title: Calls, texts & voice notes
goal: Make and take calls, deal with bad signal and missed calls, say you'll call back, and manage messages, voice notes and shared locations.
intro:
Telugu phone talk is short, fast and full of English: **కాల్ చెయ్**, **కట్ అయింది**, **సిగ్నల్ లేదు**, **లొకేషన్ షేర్ చెయ్**. The English word stays as it is and a Telugu verb (usually **చేయు**, **అవు**, **పెట్టు** or **ఇవ్వు**) carries the grammar.

You'll learn how to answer the phone, say you can't hear, promise to call back, and chase a friend who isn't replying. Two pieces of grammar make this easy: chaining actions with **-ఇ** and **-ఆక** ('do X and then Y', 'after X'), and the little time words **ఇప్పుడే** (just), **ఆల్రెడీ / అప్పుడే** (already), **ఇంకా** (still, yet) and **ఇక** (any more). You'll also meet the spoken **-ట్లేదు** ending: *ఎత్తట్లేదు*, 'isn't picking up'.

vocab.note: The person called is in the dative: అమ్మకి ఫోన్ చేశా = I called Mum

grammar.title: Do X and then Y: -ఇ, -ఆక and -అకుండా
grammar.body:
**-ఇ, 'having done'** (Unit 16) chains actions done by the **same person**; only the last verb carries tense: *భోజనం చేసి ఫోన్ చేస్తా* (I'll eat and then call). Learn the forms: చేయు → **చేసి**, వెళ్ళు → **వెళ్ళి**, రా → **వచ్చి**, చూడు → **చూసి**, ఇవ్వు → **ఇచ్చి**, తిను → **తిని**, అవు → **అయి**. With **చూడు** after it, it means 'try': *ఫోన్ చేసి చూడు* (try calling).

**-ఆక, 'after'**: past stem + **-ఆక**: *వచ్చాక* (after coming), *చేశాక*, *వెళ్ళాక*, *తిన్నాక*, *అయ్యాక* (after it's over). Unlike -ఇ, the two halves can have **different subjects**: *నువ్వు వచ్చాక మాట్లాడదాం* (after you come, let's talk). The careful form is *వచ్చిన తర్వాత*.

**-అకుండా, 'without'**: stem + **-అకుండా**: *చెప్పకుండా* (without saying), *చూడకుండా* (without looking).

The trap: *నువ్వు ఇంటికి చేరి నేను ఫోన్ చేస్తా* is wrong, because -ఇ needs one subject. Say *నువ్వు ఇంటికి చేరాక నేను ఫోన్ చేస్తా*.

examples.en: I'll call you once I get home.
He read the message and replied straight away.
Let's talk after you get here.
He hung up without saying anything.

grammar.title: Just, already, still, yet, any more
grammar.body:
**Just**: **ఇప్పుడే** + past: *ఇప్పుడే చూశా* (I've just seen it).

**Already**: **ఆల్రెడీ** or **ఇప్పటికే** + past, neutral: *ఆల్రెడీ పంపా* (I've already sent it). **అప్పుడే** is 'already' with surprise, 'so soon!': *అప్పుడే వచ్చేశావా?* (you're here already?). The completive **-ఏసు** (*చేసేశా*, *వచ్చేశా*) often adds the sense of 'all done'.

**Still**: **ఇంకా** + a positive verb: *ఇంకా ఆఫీసులోనే ఉన్నా* (I'm still at the office).

**Not yet**: **ఇంకా** + negative past **-లేదు**: *ఇంకా రాలేదు* (hasn't come yet). On its own, 'not yet' is *ఇంకా లేదు*.

**Not any more**: **ఇక** + a negative: *ఇక ఫోన్ చేయను* (I won't call any more). *ఇక చాలు!* = that's enough now!

**Isn't …ing (right now)**: in speech, stem + **-ట్లేదు**: *ఎత్తట్లేదు* (isn't picking up), *వినిపించట్లేదు* (I can't hear), *పని చేయట్లేదు* (isn't working). The careful form is *-డం లేదు*: *ఎత్తడం లేదు*.

examples.en: I'm not calling him any more.
It's ringing, but nobody's picking up.

dialogue.title: Bad signal
dialogue.setting: Hyderabad. Divya finally gets through to Sai, who is on the metro, about their friend Keerthi's birthday.

lines.speaker: Sai
lines.en: Yeah, Divya! Can you hear me?

lines.speaker: Sai
lines.en: I'm on the metro, the signal keeps going... now?

lines.speaker: Divya
lines.native: ఇప్పుడు ఓకే. ఉదయం నుంచి నాలుగు సార్లు కాల్ చేశా, ఎందుకు ఎత్తలేదు?
lines.roman: ippuḍu ōkē. udayam nunchi nālugu sārlu kāl chēshā, enduku ettalēdu?

lines.speaker: Sai
lines.native: సారీ, మీటింగ్‌లో ఉన్నా, ఫోన్ సైలెంట్‌లో ఉంది. ఇప్పుడే నీ మిస్డ్ కాల్స్ చూశా.
lines.roman: sārī, mīṭiṅglō unnā, phōn sailenṭlō undi. ippuḍē nī misḍ kāls chūshā.
lines.en: Sorry, I was in a meeting and my phone was on silent. I've only just seen your missed calls.

lines.speaker: Divya
lines.native: సరే, విను. ఈ సాయంత్రం కీర్తి బర్త్‌డే పార్టీ, గుర్తుందా?
lines.roman: sarē, vinu. ī sāyantram kīrti barthḍē pārṭī, gurtundā?
lines.en: OK, listen. It's Keerthi's birthday party this evening, remember?

lines.speaker: Divya
lines.native: జూబ్లీ హిల్స్‌లో ఏదో కేఫ్. గ్రూప్‌లో ఆల్రెడీ లొకేషన్ షేర్ చేశా, చూసుకో.
lines.roman: jūblī hilslō ēdō kēph. grūplō ālreḍī lokēṣan ṣēr chēshā, chūsukō.
lines.en: Some café in Jubilee Hills. I've already shared the location on the group, check it.

lines.speaker: Sai
lines.native: సరే, ఆఫీసు అయ్యాక నేరుగా వచ్చేస్తా. హలో? దివ్యా?
lines.roman: sarē, āphīsu ayyāka nērugā vachchēstā. halō? divyā?
lines.en: OK, I'll come straight after work. Hello? Divya?

lines.speaker: Sai
lines.native: సిగ్నల్ పోయింది. లొకేషన్ చూశా, ఏడింటికి అక్కడ ఉంటా.
lines.roman: signal pōyindi. lokēṣan chūshā, ēḍiṇṭiki akkaḍa uṇṭā.
lines.en: (Voice note) Lost the signal. Saw the location, I'll be there at seven.

lines.speaker: Divya
lines.native: ఓకే. ఈసారి లేట్ చేస్తే నీ ఫోన్ నేనే స్విచ్ ఆఫ్ చేస్తా!
lines.roman: ōkē. īsāri lēṭ chēstē nī phōn nēnē svich āph chēstā!
lines.en: (Voice note) OK. If you're late this time, I'll switch your phone off myself!

culture: Telugu speakers answer the phone with *హలో*, and when they know who's calling, simply *ఆ, చెప్పు* ('yeah, go on') or, to an elder, *చెప్పండి*. Opening with a blunt *ఎవరు?* is common but can sound rude from a learner, so *ఎవరు మాట్లాడుతున్నారు?* is safer. The **missed call** is a whole language: one ring can mean 'I've reached', 'call me back' or 'I'm downstairs'. Voice notes are hugely popular, especially with parents and grandparents who find typing in Telugu script slow. Among young people, chats are mostly typed in **Telugu written in English letters** ('em chestunnav?', 'vastunna ra'), sprinkled with English. Expect a family WhatsApp group full of good-morning flowers and festival greetings, and expect to be added to one.

tip.title: On the phone
tip.body:
- Answer with **హలో**, or if you know the caller **ఆ, చెప్పు** / **చెప్పండి** 'go on'.
- Call = **ఫోన్ చేయు** / **కాల్ చేయు**, and the person called is in the dative: **అమ్మకి** ఫోన్ చేశా.
- Pick up = **ఫోన్ ఎత్తు** · hang up = **కట్ చేయు** · ring = **రింగ్ అవు**.

sentences.en: Did you call Mum?
Call me tonight.
The phone's ringing, pick up!
Yeah, go on, man, what is it?

He hung up in a temper.

sentences.native: హలో, ఎవరు మాట్లాడుతున్నారు? మీ నంబరు సేవ్ చేయలేదు.
sentences.roman: halō, evaru māṭlāḍutunnāru? mī nambaru sēv chēyalēdu.
sentences.en: Hello, who's speaking? I haven't saved your number.

However many times I try, I can't get through.
Why didn't you pick up? Were you busy?

tip.title: Isn't …ing: -ట్లేదు
tip.body:
- Spoken 'isn't …ing (right now)' = stem + **-ట్లేదు**: వినిపించ**ట్లేదు**, పని చేయ**ట్లేదు**. Careful form: వినిపించడం లేదు.
- **వినిపించు** works like కనిపించు: the hearer is in the dative: **నాకు** వినిపించట్లేదు.
- Is it …ing? **-తోందా?**: వినిపిస్తోందా?

sentences.en: I can't hear you.
The signal isn't good here.
The network isn't working.
Can you hear me now?
His phone's coming up as switched off.
My battery's dying, let's talk later.
Speak up a bit, I can't hear.

tip.title: And then, after, without: -ఇ, -ఆక, -అకుండా
tip.body:
- Same person does both: **-ఇ**: భోజనం **చేసి** ఫోన్ చేస్తా.
- After (any subject): past stem + **-ఆక**: నువ్వు **వచ్చాక**, మీటింగ్ **అయ్యాక**.
- Without: **-అకుండా**: **చెప్పకుండా**.
- Try doing: **-ఇ చూడు**: ఫోన్ చేసి చూడు.

sentences.en: I'll have lunch and then call you back.
I'll call you back after the meeting.

sentences.native: నువ్వు ఇంటికి చేరాక నాకు మిస్డ్ కాల్ ఇవ్వు.
sentences.roman: nuvvu iṇṭiki chērāka nāku misḍ kāl ivvu.
sentences.en: Give me a missed call when you get home.

tip.title: Just, already, still, not yet
tip.body:
- Just: **ఇప్పుడే** + past · already: **ఆల్రెడీ** + past · already?! (so soon): **అప్పుడే**.
- Still: **ఇంకా** + positive: ఇంకా ఆఫీసులోనే ఉన్నాడు.
- Not yet: **ఇంకా** + **-లేదు**: ఇంకా రిప్లై **రాలేదు**.
- Not any more: **ఇక** + negative: **ఇక** పెట్టను.

sentences.en: I've only just seen your message, sorry.
It's been two hours, still no reply.
I've already put the tickets on the group.
You're here already?
Apparently he's still at the office.
I'm not posting on that group any more.
Did you see my message? Why didn't you reply?

sentences.native: మా ఇంటి వాట్సాప్ గ్రూప్‌లో రోజూ వంద మెసేజ్‌లు వస్తాయి.

lessons.title: Voice notes, locations and video calls

tip.title: English word + చేయు / పెట్టు
tip.body:
- The English word never changes; the Telugu verb carries the grammar: **షేర్ చెయ్**, **టైప్ చేస్తున్నా**, **వీడియో కాల్ చేయనా?**
- Post or send in a chat: **పెట్టు**: వాయిస్ నోట్ **పెడతా**, గ్రూప్‌లో **పెట్టా**.
- Check it yourself: **చూసుకో**.
